requirements.statement: A changelog SHALL be generated from git over an explicit range, grouped by Conventional Commit type, and written to the changelog folder by one command
requirements.basis: Measured. `wc3ctl changelog` takes a from and a to ref, reads the git log between them, groups by Conventional Commit type and writes the markdown to the changelog folder. The committed entries read as that shape, Added, Changed and Fixed headings over subject lines

requirements.statement: The changelog SHALL carry the requirement IDs a commit names, SHALL put a breaking change in its own section, SHALL list a commit it could not parse, and SHALL fail when a commit does not follow the convention
requirements.basis: Design decision. Today the subject is parsed and a non-conforming subject falls under `other`, while the `!` marker and any requirement reference are ignored (G-37)

requirements.statement: The reference documents SHALL be regenerated by one command, and CI SHALL fail when either is stale
requirements.basis: Measured. `wc3ctl docs all --force` regenerates both documents, and `Command_reference_matches_the_live_tree` and `Mcp_reference_matches_the_live_tool_surface` render the live tree in memory and report the first differing line against the committed file, so a stale document fails the test run CI already executes

requirements.statement: One command SHALL build, publish and verify every front end into a fresh folder, swap it in, and print the timestamp of every published exe
requirements.basis: Measured. `publish-all.ps1` publishes and prints the timestamps. It does not run the tests or regenerate the docs

requirements.statement: A watch command SHALL rebuild, run the hermetic suite, regenerate the docs and publish when a source file changes, and SHALL refuse to publish when a gate fails
requirements.basis: Design decision. No watch exists today (G-39)

requirements.statement: A release-readiness command SHALL run the build, the hermetic suite, the docs guard, the surface audit, the parity check and the publish verification, and SHALL print one verdict with one exit code
requirements.basis: Design decision. The parts exist and no command folds them (G-40)

requirements.statement: Every automation command SHALL answer `--json` with a stable object, so an agent can drive the same loop a person drives
requirements.basis: Design decision. `changelog` and `ci` answer JSON. `docs` and the publish script do not (G-43)

requirements.statement: A published binary SHALL be verified by starting it and reading its version and, for the server, its tool count, and the check SHALL fail on a stale version or timestamp
requirements.basis: Measured. The release smoke does this once. The local publish does not (G-42)

requirements.statement: A release SHALL be one tag, one version, one changelog entry and one handoff to the mirror, and the changelog entry SHALL be committed before the tag
requirements.basis: Measured. The tag and the handoff are automated. The changelog entry is not part of the gate (G-38)

requirements.statement: The changelog SHALL be checked for staleness against the commits it covers, the way the reference documents are checked, so a release cannot ship notes that miss a commit
requirements.basis: Design decision. Nothing checks the committed changelog (G-44)

requirements.statement: The release SHALL write a machine-readable record of the source commit, the artifact digests and the tag, and a published version SHALL resolve to that record
requirements.basis: Design decision. The npm 0.5.19 artifact has no tag that explains it

requirements.statement: The server SHALL answer every protocol revision it claims, each proven by a test, and SHALL state what an unknown offer resolves to
requirements.basis: Measured. `ProtocolRevisionTests` drives 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25, each echoes, unknown offers resolve to 2025-11-25, and the tool count holds at 275

requirements.statement: The SDK version SHALL be pinned, and an upgrade SHALL include a protocol test run and a note in the release
requirements.basis: Measured. The package is pinned at 1.4.1 and the transitive host packages are isolated to this exe

requirements.statement: A tool rename SHALL follow the alias window in SUR-03, and the removed name SHALL be listed in the release note that removes it
requirements.basis: Design decision. A client's saved prompt is the reason

requirements.statement: A result field SHALL change only additively within a major version, and a removed field SHALL be announced one minor release before
requirements.basis: Design decision. A caller writes against names

requirements.statement: A tool SHALL keep working when the target build or the game install is absent, where it does not need them, and the failure mode SHALL be stated
requirements.basis: Measured. Map tools work without the game and base-data tools do not

requirements.statement: The server SHALL record the minimum client capability it relies on, which is tools. Resources and prompts SHALL degrade gracefully when a client does not offer them, and the server SHALL NOT require sampling, elicitation, roots or a completion handler
requirements.basis: Design decision. A client that offers only tools still gets a usable server

requirements.statement: The server SHALL publish a tested protocol revision matrix naming the revision, the SDK version, the fields emitted and the features an older client loses
requirements.basis: Measured. `ProtocolRevisionTests` pins the matrix and the item surface at the negotiated revision

requirements.statement: The generated MCP reference SHALL include each tool's family, description, every parameter with type and default, the result shape, the error codes and the hints, and CI SHALL fail when the committed file is stale
requirements.basis: Measured. The file is generated and guarded, and it carries no parameters and no result shape

requirements.statement: This specification SHALL be versioned, SHALL carry a change log, and SHALL name the build it describes
requirements.basis: Measured. The cover and the footer carry version 1.29, the change log table names every revision with its date and its scope, and section 3.1 names the build the document describes, 275 tools from wc3ctl 0.4.13 at protocol 2025-11-25

requirements.statement: The README SHALL state only facts that a command or a file in the repository proves, and a test or a script SHALL check the counts it quotes
requirements.basis: Measured. `tools/check_counts.py` parses the tool count from the README, the requirement, group and check counts from section 2 and the README, and the gap-row count from the README, and compares them with the live exe and `requirements.json`. It exits 2 on a drift and the PDF build refuses to render

requirements.statement: Every claim in a release note SHALL name the requirement it satisfies or the defect it closes
requirements.basis: Not implemented. The release notes name tools, behaviours and measurements, and never a requirement id or a defect number, so a reader cannot tell which rule a change serves

requirements.statement: A breaking change to a tool name, a parameter or a result field SHALL be stated in the release note, in the deprecated tool's description and in this specification
requirements.basis: Not implemented. No release note marks a breaking change, no tool description carries a deprecation note, and nothing in the changelogs names the three places a break has to appear

requirements.statement: A requirement whose basis claims a protocol rule, a client behaviour or an external measurement SHALL cite the source in Appendix D, and a requirement with no such source SHALL be labelled a design decision
requirements.basis: Design decision. A claim about the protocol that names no page cannot be checked by its reader

requirements.statement: The PDF SHALL offer a light printing edition with larger table text, and the cover statistics SHALL be generated from the document rather than typed
requirements.basis: Measured. `build_pdf.py --light` renders the same source with a light palette and 8.6pt table text, 73 pages against the dark edition's 63, and a mean page luminance of 189 against 13. The cover statistics are computed from the document by `document_facts`

requirements.statement: The initialize instructions SHALL state the product and version, the target build and its source, whether game data is available, the three safety rules (read before write, never overwrite the input, chain edits on the output), and that `quickstart` routes a broad request. The whole field SHALL stay under 1,000 characters
requirements.basis: Measured. The field is 405 characters and carries every one of those facts

requirements.statement: `quickstart` SHALL cover every family and SHALL return, for each workflow, the prompt name, the tools in order and the CLI equivalent
requirements.basis: Measured. Twelve workflows, and every one of the eleven families is named by at least one of them. Each workflow carries its prompt name, and `Every_family_is_reachable_from_a_quickstart_workflow` fails when a family has no workflow, when a workflow names a tool that is not on the surface, or when it names a prompt the server does not serve

requirements.statement: A `tool_help` tool SHALL return the full description, every parameter with its default and legal values, the result shape, the error codes and an example call for one named tool
requirements.basis: Design decision. With descriptions capped at 600 characters, the long form needs one place a caller can ask for

requirements.statement: The catalog resource, `wc3ctl mcp tools`, `mcp_audit_annotations` and the live `tools/list` SHALL be computed from one reflection call, and a test SHALL compare all four
requirements.basis: Measured. This holds today. It is the property that stops documentation drift

requirements.statement: An error for a missing capability SHOULD name the tool that has it, for example a call to read a replay from `search` naming `replay_summary`
requirements.basis: Design decision. The surface is too large to browse and an error is a free routing hint

requirements.statement: `quickstart` with no arguments, and the initialize instructions, SHALL answer with a short orientation rather than a required-parameter error. A tool whose schema requires a map SHALL still require it
requirements.basis: Design decision. A fresh client often calls the first tool it sees with nothing

requirements.statement: Every environment variable the server reads SHALL be listed in one table with its effect, its default and its precedence
requirements.basis: Design decision. `WC3_GAME_DIR`, `WC3_TARGET_BUILD`, `WC3_MCP_NPX`, `WC3_MCP_LOG` and `CODEX_HOME` are read in different files

requirements.statement: The precedence of each variable against its tool argument and its saved setting SHALL be tested, including the placeholder case
requirements.basis: Measured. `McpEnvPrecedenceTests` pins all seven tiers, the game directory argument over the environment, the environment when no argument is given, the target argument over the environment over the settings file, the source each tier reports, and both placeholder cases, an unfilled `${...}` in the argument and in the environment, which count as unset

requirements.statement: An undocumented environment variable SHALL NOT change behaviour, and a variable read for a test SHALL be namespaced and listed
requirements.basis: Design decision. A hidden switch is a behaviour nobody can reproduce

requirements.statement: On start the server SHALL write one line to stderr with the product, version, the newest protocol revision the build speaks, tool count, target, game directory and profile
requirements.basis: Measured. `BuildStartLine` writes `wc3ctl 0.4.13  protocol 2025-11-25  tools 275  target Beta-ROC-v1.00 (settings)  game 3.0.1.24371  profile full` at 0.31 seconds, and the line costs 0.03 seconds of the cold start

requirements.statement: `WC3_MCP_LOG` SHALL set the log level, default to warn, and never accept a value that turns on per-call payload logging
requirements.basis: Measured. `McpLogLevel` maps `error`, `warn`, `info` and `debug`, and an unknown value falls back to warn. The published exe writes nothing to stderr at the default, 16 lines at `info` and 24 at `debug`, and every line goes to stderr

requirements.statement: A configuration file SHALL NOT be needed. The server SHALL work with no file, no environment variable and no game install, for the tools that do not need them
requirements.basis: Measured. This is the current behaviour and it is the property that makes a one-line install work

requirements.statement: An expected failure SHALL return a tool error with a one-line message, and SHALL NOT crash the process or return a stack trace
requirements.basis: Measured. A call for a map that is not there returns `isError` true and the single line `map not found: Z:/nowhere/missing.w3x`, with no stack frame and the server still answering the next call. A call that fails schema validation returns a one-line message too

requirements.statement: Every tool error SHALL carry a stable code, the message, and a next step where one exists, as structured content beside the text
requirements.basis: Design decision. A code lets a caller branch, and a next step turns a dead end into one retry

requirements.statement: The error code set SHALL be documented in one place and tested, and a new code SHALL fail the test until it is listed
requirements.basis: Design decision. An undocumented code is a string a client cannot rely on

requirements.statement: A missing Warcraft III install SHALL NOT fail a tool that does not need it, and a tool that needs it SHALL say so before it reads the map
requirements.basis: Half measured. A map tool works with `WC3_GAME_DIR` pointed at nothing. The tools that lose a check say so in the result rather than before reading, and `gamedata_enum` with no schemas found returns `entries: []` with no note that it searched nothing

requirements.statement: A partial success SHALL be reported as partial, with the items that failed and the reason, and SHALL NOT be reported as success
requirements.basis: Not implemented. The batch tools refuse rather than report a partial, so no result carries a partial shape and no test pins the rule

requirements.statement: An error message SHALL name the path, the input and the rule that refused, and SHALL NOT include file contents, a configuration value or a token
requirements.basis: Not tested. A map error names the path and the rule, but a call that fails schema validation returns a message naming none of them, and no test scans error text for content that should not travel

requirements.statement: A call that names an unknown tool SHALL be answered by the protocol layer with the unknown-tool error, and the server SHALL NOT invent a tool or guess a near name
requirements.basis: Measured. `no_such_tool_xyz` is answered with `Unknown tool: 'no_such_tool_xyz'` at the protocol layer. The server registers no dispatcher of its own, so there is no code path that could replace or soften that answer

requirements.statement: The server SHALL take its product id, its registered server name and its version from assembly metadata written at build time, and SHALL NOT hardcode them in source or branch on a repository name
requirements.basis: Measured. The identity today comes from `McpProductId` and `McpServerName` in `Wc3.Mcp.csproj`, overridden by each repository's `Directory.Build.props`, so one source builds `wc3ctl` and `wc3-mcp`

requirements.statement: One product version SHALL be the source of every version a caller can read, which is the exe, `version_info`, the npm package, the `.mcpb` manifest, `server.json` and the release tag. The release SHALL refuse a tag that differs from the exe. A committed check SHALL report every place the values disagree, even between releases
requirements.basis: Measured. Six live artifacts carry five disagreeing values today, 0.4.13, 0.5.16, 0.5.8, 0.3.0 in two files, and 0.5.19 on npm. The release aligns them, the tree does not

requirements.statement: `version_info` SHALL return the product id, the server name, the version, the git short hash, the UTC build time, the MCP protocol revision and the SDK version
requirements.basis: Design decision. A caller diagnosing a client problem needs the whole build identity in one call, not four

requirements.statement: The registered server name SHALL be stable for a product, `wc3ctl` for the CLI and `wc3` for the public server, and SHALL be the name used to remove or reinstall it
requirements.basis: Measured. Setup writes the name, then removes by the same name. A name that moved would leave a stale entry behind

requirements.statement: A build without git SHALL report `nogit` and an unknown time rather than a git error message, and the fallback SHALL be tested
requirements.basis: Measured. The build target validates the hash shape for exactly this reason

requirements.statement: The protocol revision and SDK version SHALL be visible without reading the project file, through `version_info` and the diagnostics tool
requirements.basis: Design decision. A client bug is often a protocol mismatch, and the build is the only place it can be seen

requirements.statement: Diagnostics SHALL go to stderr with a level, and SHALL NOT interleave with the protocol stream
requirements.basis: Measured. Diagnostics arrived on stderr with their level prefix, `dbug` and `info` observed in one capture, and no diagnostic reached stdout, which the same capture parsed as pure JSON

requirements.statement: A call that exceeds 2 seconds SHALL log its tool name, its duration and its result size to stderr
requirements.basis: Not implemented. The only per-call line is the SDK's completion record, which names the tool and its `isError` flag and carries neither a duration nor a result size, so the one line this requirement exists for does not exist

requirements.statement: A log line SHALL NOT contain map contents, script text, a string-table value or a file body. It MAY contain a path, a size, a digest and a duration
requirements.basis: Not tested. The records observed carried tool names and an `isError` flag, and no test fails when a log line carries content it should not

requirements.statement: A tool error SHALL be logged once at warn with its code, and SHALL NOT be logged again by the generic handler as an unknown failure
requirements.basis: Not implemented. A failing call is logged once by the generic handler as an unhandled exception at debug, not at warn, and the line carries no error code

requirements.statement: `map` SHALL accept either a map file (`.w3x` or `.w3m`) or an unpacked map folder, and the parameter description SHALL say which a tool takes. A file's extension SHALL be checked before the archive is opened
requirements.basis: Measured. `LoadMap` accepts a folder and checks the extension only for a file, and the folder map and Lua suites pass on folder fixtures. Seven of the 202 `map` parameter descriptions say a folder is accepted, so the wording half of the requirement is not done

requirements.statement: The game directory SHALL resolve from the tool argument, then `WC3_GAME_DIR`, then auto-detection. A value holding an unfilled placeholder SHALL count as unset
requirements.basis: Measured. `McpEnvPrecedenceTests` proves the argument wins over the environment, the environment is used when no argument is given, and an unfilled `${...}` in either place counts as unset rather than as a folder name

requirements.statement: The target build SHALL resolve from the tool argument, then `WC3_TARGET_BUILD`, then the saved setting, then the default, and `target_get` SHALL report which source won
requirements.basis: Measured. The same test class proves the argument beats the environment, the environment beats the settings file, the settings file is used when both are clear, and each tier reports its own source

requirements.statement: A tool that needs game data SHALL state in its description what it returns without it, and its result SHALL mark any degraded field rather than returning an empty value that reads as real
requirements.basis: Half met. `placed_fix_refs` says a base-game check was skipped, which is the shape the rule wants, and the rest of the game directory tools return unmarked results

requirements.statement: A parameter value outside its legal set SHALL be refused with an error that lists the legal set. No parameter SHALL be accepted and ignored
requirements.basis: Half met. `object_list` refuses an unknown kind with `expected one of: unit

requirements.statement: `out_path` SHALL be required where the output is a different artifact type, such as a PNG, CSV, OBJ, atlas or report, and optional with a stated default where the output is an edited map
requirements.basis: Measured. 98 writing tools require `out_path`, the 12 that make it optional are the map edits and each states the default in its own description, a sibling `.edited` copy, and a tool whose output is a folder takes `out_dir` instead

requirements.statement: A coordinate SHALL state its unit and frame in the parameter description, either world units, terrain cells, pathing cells or corners, and a rotation SHALL state radians or degrees
requirements.basis: Measured. All 13 coordinate parameters say world coordinate or world units, and all three rotation parameters say radians and name the map's own convention

requirements.statement: An array parameter SHALL have a stated maximum, and a call above it SHALL be refused rather than truncated
requirements.basis: Half met. `object_batch_set` states its limit, at most 500 edits. The other eight array parameters state no maximum and none is proven to refuse an oversized call

requirements.statement: A path parameter SHALL accept forward slashes on Windows, and an internal archive path SHALL accept either slash and normalize it
requirements.basis: Measured. `file_get_text` returns the same bytes for `war3map.j` and `(listfile)` written with either slash, a name that is not in the map is refused by name, and every filesystem path in this document's measurements is written with forward slashes on Windows

requirements.statement: The published server SHALL be self-contained for win-x64, with `CascLib.dll` and the `context/` folder beside the exe, and SHALL start without a .NET install
requirements.basis: Measured. `dist-mcp` carries `coreclr.dll`, `System.Private.CoreLib.dll` and `hostfxr.dll`, so the runtime travels with the exe, and `CascLib.dll` and `context/` sit beside it. Every capture in this document started that exe with no runtime on the path
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The npm launcher SHALL cache the binary per version under the user's local app data, verify the release archive against its published SHA-256, refuse a mismatch, and never fail an npm install when the network is down
requirements.basis: Measured. `ensure-binary.js` caches under `LOCALAPPDATA`, downloads the `.sha256` beside the zip, compares and throws `checksum mismatch` on a difference. The postinstall path catches every failure, writes it to stderr and returns 0, so a restricted build machine installs the package without the binary
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The npm launcher SHALL write nothing to stdout except its own version, because stdout is the protocol stream once the exe starts
requirements.basis: Measured. The only `process.stdout.write` in the launcher is the version line, and every other message, the preload skip, the download and the start failure, goes to stderr
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The `.mcpb` manifest version SHALL be set from the tag at release, validated with the official validator, and packed with the exe and its dependencies
requirements.basis: Measured. The release workflow copies the published folder into the bundle stage, rewrites the manifest version from the tag, validates with `@anthropic-ai/mcpb`, then packs and hashes the result
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: `server.json` SHALL be filled at release with the version, the bundle URL and the bundle SHA-256, and published only once per tag
requirements.basis: Measured. The registry job fills `server.json` from the release values, validates it with `mcp-publisher` and publishes through OIDC, which is what makes it once per tag rather than once per run
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The release SHALL start the published exe, ask it its version and refuse the release when that differs from the tag
requirements.basis: Measured. The workflow starts the published exe and compares its version with the tag, and the smoke script drives it over stdio, so a release cannot ship an exe that never answered
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The export SHALL take files from a named commit, refuse a path with uncommitted changes, refuse a Windows profile path or a private identity, and leave the target repository's own files alone
requirements.basis: Measured. `scripts/export-wc3-mcp.py` implements all four rules

requirements.statement: A release SHALL publish into an empty folder and swap it in, never publish over a previous one
requirements.basis: Measured. Each target publishes into a fresh stage folder, and the self-updater stages beside the install and swaps, which is the same rule at run time. The stale `System.Text.Json.dll` incident is why the comment sits in the workflow
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: On a non-Windows or non-x64 platform the server SHALL fail with one sentence that names the supported target, not a missing native library trace
requirements.basis: Not implemented. The tree holds no platform check, and the launcher has none either, so a Linux or ARM user gets the operating system's own failure for a Windows executable rather than a sentence naming `win-x64`

requirements.statement: Old cached versions SHALL be pruned to two, and a failed prune because a client holds the exe SHALL NOT fail the launch
requirements.basis: Measured. `pruneOldVersions` keeps the current version and the newest other one, and a delete that fails with `EBUSY` or `EPERM` is ignored while every other error is raised
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: The release assets SHALL include a `.sha256` for the zip and the bundle, and the installer SHALL verify it before unpacking
requirements.basis: Measured. The release writes a `.sha256` beside every zip, the bundle and the schemas archive, and the launcher verifies the zip against it before it unpacks
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: An update SHALL replace a running install by renaming a locked exe or DLL to a `.old` sibling and copying the new file in, so a client holding the old binary open does not have to be closed first, and the `.old` copy SHALL be removable on the next run
requirements.basis: Measured. `SelfUpdateCommand` moves a locked target to a `*.old` sibling, copies the new file in, and deletes every `*.old` under the install on the next run
requirements.test: read from the release workflow and the launcher

requirements.statement: Every published artifact SHALL name its source commit, its artifact digest and the tag it was built from, and a version number alone SHALL NOT be treated as provenance
requirements.basis: Measured. npm `latest` is 0.5.19 while the newest tag is v0.5.16, created on 20 October 2026

requirements.statement: A cold start to the first initialize reply SHALL be under 1 second on a warm disk, and the surface SHALL NOT be recomputed per session
requirements.basis: Measured. The lazy holds, and the cold start is 1.2 seconds on a warm disk on the development machine, four runs between 1.15 and 1.27 after the first. The start line reaches stderr at 0.31 seconds and costs 0.03 seconds, measured with the line suppressed

requirements.statement: `tools/list` SHALL answer in under 100 ms after start
requirements.basis: Design decision. It is reflection over a fixed list, and a client calls it on every launch

requirements.statement: A call SHALL load each input once. A tool SHALL NOT load the same map twice, and `LoadMap` SHALL be the only entry point
requirements.basis: Measured. `port_unit` deliberately loads the source and the target once each and never feeds output back

requirements.statement: A tool expected to exceed 2 seconds SHALL report progress and SHALL observe cancellation. The families are map optimisation, folder audits, model import and export, atlas and texture work, and the doctor repair
requirements.basis: Measured. No tool reports progress or accepts a cancellation token today, and several of these run for minutes

requirements.statement: Memory SHALL stay bounded by the largest single input plus its output, and a folder tool SHALL process one map at a time
requirements.basis: Design decision. A library of 500 maps must not be loaded at once

requirements.statement: The RAG index and the embedder SHALL load once per process and stay loaded, and a failed load SHALL fall back to lexical search rather than fail the call
requirements.basis: Measured. Both are lazy and kept. The fallback is the current behaviour

requirements.statement: A performance gate SHALL fail CI when a read-only call on the reference map regresses past a stated multiple of its baseline
requirements.basis: Design decision. `bench_perf_gate` already exists and the MCP layer is not in it

requirements.statement: The server SHALL apply explicit limits to archive entry count, decompressed bytes per entry and per call, parser depth, array size, temporary disk and child-process time, and SHALL refuse with a code before allocation
requirements.basis: Design decision. Managed code and an exception handler are not a resource bound

requirements.statement: The server SHALL state a memory budget on a named reference machine for the largest supported map, and a call that would exceed it SHALL be refused rather than attempted
requirements.basis: Design decision. PRF-05 counts the input and output and ignores parsed sections, assets, schemas and concurrent calls

requirements.statement: A prompt SHALL return guidance text and SHALL NOT read or write a map, call a tool, or change any state
requirements.basis: Measured. All thirteen methods only concatenate strings. None takes a path it opens, none calls a tool, and none touches a file, so serving one has no side effect. `Every_prompt_is_pullable_with_no_arguments_and_names_real_tools` invokes all thirteen with no arguments and gets text back

requirements.statement: There SHALL be one prompt for each workflow `quickstart` returns, so a client that can read prompts gets the same plan the routing tool describes
requirements.basis: Measured. Thirteen prompts, one per workflow, plus `audit_hero_spells`. `Every_quickstart_workflow_has_a_prompt` fails when a workflow has no prompt or when a mapped prompt has no method, so the two lists cannot drift

requirements.statement: Every prompt SHALL name the tools to call, in order, and the guard rule that applies, such as writing to a new path and never overwriting the input
requirements.basis: Measured. Each prompt returns a numbered plan, and the test fails on a prompt that names fewer than two tools, on a step list with no order, and on any name that is neither a tool nor a parameter. The writing prompts state the new path and the overwrite rule, and the read-only ones say to change nothing. This test found `place_doodad_set` in one prompt, which is not a tool, and the real name is `placed_doodad_set`

requirements.statement: A prompt argument SHALL be optional and its placeholder SHALL name what to substitute, so a prompt can be pulled before the user has chosen a map
requirements.basis: Measured. Every argument has a default, the test fails on a required one, and the text substitutes `<map>`, `the job the caller names` and similar rather than leaving a bare parameter name

requirements.statement: The prompt list SHALL be available in the catalog with its arguments, and a stale prompt that names a removed tool SHALL fail the parity test
requirements.basis: Half measured. A stale name now fails the contract test, which caught one. The prompt list is still not in the catalog resource, so a client must call prompts/list to learn what a prompt takes

requirements.statement: A successful tool call SHALL return a JSON object as its text content, and SHALL NOT return prose that a caller has to parse
requirements.basis: Measured. Every result is a POCO serialized by the SDK. The exception is a result that is genuinely a list, which SHALL be wrapped as `{ items, count }` (RES-02)

requirements.statement: Every tool SHALL publish an `outputSchema`, and SHALL return the same object as `structuredContent`. The text content SHALL stay for a client that does not read structured content
requirements.basis: Measured. No tool publishes an output schema, so a client cannot validate a result or discover its shape without calling the tool

requirements.statement: No single result SHALL exceed 256 KB of structured JSON, excluding binary content blocks, which RES-05 bounds separately at 1 MB. A list tool SHALL accept `limit` and `offset`, default to a bounded page, and state the total and the next offset. A capped result SHALL say it is capped
requirements.basis: Design decision. A caller that fills its context with one result cannot finish the task, and a silent cap reads as the whole answer

requirements.statement: `file_get_text` SHALL decode with an explicit encoding, report that encoding and whether it was chosen or assumed, count the bytes the decoder had to replace, and report a `lossy` flag, SHALL refuse a lossy decode unless `allow_lossy` is true, and a separate `file_extract` tool SHALL write the raw bytes to disk. Text that is valid under the selected encoding, including non-ASCII text, SHALL NOT be reported as lossy
requirements.basis: Measured. `FileEditCommand.ReadText` decodes UTF-8 without throwing on invalid bytes, so a Cyrillic script comes back with replacement characters. The project record shows the resulting corruption when such text is written back

requirements.statement: Binary content SHALL travel as a saved path, a resource link or an image content block under 1 MB. A larger payload SHALL be a path, never inline base64
requirements.basis: Measured. `render_model` inlines a PNG up to 1 MB and reports the path, which is the right shape

requirements.statement: A result field SHALL carry the same name and meaning as the CLI's `--json` output for the same operation
requirements.basis: Measured. Both front ends serialize the same POCO, so this holds today and is easy to break

requirements.statement: An enum SHALL serialize as its name, not its number
requirements.basis: Measured. `JsonOptions` adds `JsonStringEnumConverter`, and a placed unit's scale needed its own converter

requirements.statement: A result field SHALL be camel case, stable within a major version, and additive only. A field SHALL NOT be renamed or removed without a major version
requirements.basis: Design decision. A caller writes code against these names

requirements.statement: A tool that allocates an identifier, such as a rawcode or a creation number, SHALL produce the same identifier for the same inputs and the same starting map, so a test can assert it
requirements.basis: Design decision. A random allocator makes the write sweep flaky and makes a caller's retry produce a second object

requirements.statement: A paged result SHALL use `returnedCount` for the page size, `totalCount` for the total, `hasMore` for whether another page exists and `nextOffset` for the next page. It SHALL NOT use a bare `count`, which a caller reads as the total
requirements.basis: Design decision. A caller reading `count` as the total is the common mistake with a paged result

requirements.statement: A result with more than one input or output SHALL report each with a role, a path and a digest, and SHALL keep `savedTo` as the primary output for the existing clients
requirements.basis: Design decision. A port reads two maps and a model export writes three files

requirements.statement: Each bundled reference document SHALL be served whole as a markdown resource, with a name, a description and its size
requirements.basis: Half met. Both documents are served whole with a name, a description and `text/markdown`. Neither reports a size

requirements.statement: Each document SHALL also be served as section resources through a URI template, so a client can read one heading by title rather than the whole file
requirements.basis: Design decision. Reading one ability's section should not cost the whole 300 KB document

requirements.statement: `wc3://tools` SHALL be generated from the live surface by the same reflection the tools use, and SHALL include each tool's family, aliases, input schema and hints
requirements.basis: Half measured. The resource is generated from the same reflection and now carries each tool's family and its four hints. Aliases and the input schema are still missing, so the client still needs tools/list to see arguments.

requirements.statement: This specification SHALL be served as `wc3://spec`, so a client can quote the rule it is following
requirements.basis: Design decision. A client that explains why it refused a call is more useful than one that silently refuses

requirements.statement: Every resource SHALL report its MIME type, its byte size and a SHA-256 in its metadata, and a read SHALL return the same bytes as the file beside the exe
requirements.basis: Half met. Every resource reports its MIME type. None reports a byte size or a SHA-256, so a client cannot tell a truncated copy from the shipped one

requirements.statement: The semantic index SHALL be opt-in. `docs_search` SHALL work lexically with no download, and `rag_status` SHALL report what is installed before anything is fetched
requirements.basis: Measured. With `W3C_RAG_HOME` pointed at an empty folder, `rag_status` reports `modelPresent` false and `indexPresent` false, `docs_search` answers in `lexical` mode with 8 matches over the two documents, and no model folder is created, so nothing was fetched

requirements.statement: A cached result SHALL be keyed by the content digest of its input, the options, the target build and the tool version, and a changed input SHALL invalidate it
requirements.basis: Design decision. The doctor cache is keyed by path, so a file edited at the same path is served a stale verdict

requirements.statement: Each bundled skill document SHALL be served as a resource and as a section resource through a URI template, with the size and digest RSC-05 requires, read from the installed folder and never from a caller path
requirements.basis: Design decision. A skill is the same kind of artifact as the two reference documents, and a client that can read one procedure whole can follow it without a prompt

requirements.statement: Every tool SHALL set all four annotation hints explicitly. An unset hint SHALL fail the annotation audit
requirements.basis: Measured. Every one of the 275 tools declares all four hints, the seven writing tools that left `destructiveHint` unset now declare false, and the audit reports an unset hint per tool by name

requirements.statement: `readOnlyHint` true SHALL mean the call writes no byte anywhere in the user's workspace. A tool that writes a PNG, a CSV, a report or a temp map SHALL NOT claim to be read-only
requirements.basis: Measured. Five writing tools said read-only in their description, `mpq_extract_all`, `terrain_export_heightmap`, `pathing_export_png`, `asset_thumbnails` and `asset_convert_batch`, and all five now say what they write and that the input is untouched. The audit fails any writing tool whose description carries the word

requirements.statement: `destructiveHint` true SHALL mean the call can discard map content that cannot be recovered from its output, such as a removed placement, object, region, trigger, variable, sound or archive entry. A tool that only adds, rebuilds or copies SHALL declare false. A transformation that discards information in its output, such as lossy model compression or a texture re-encode, SHALL state what it discards and SHALL declare the hint for that loss. Replacing an existing destination is a separate fact and is governed by `overwrite`
requirements.basis: Measured. Eleven tools declare it true, including `mpq_remove` and `mpq_remove_many`, which remove archive entries and are the kind of loss this rule names. The seven that left it unset, `gamedata_export_schemas`, `pathing_export_png`, `terrain_export_heightmap`, `model_primitive`, `model_squish`, `target_set` and `rag_install`, all declare false, which matches the definition because each writes a new artifact and discards no map content

requirements.statement: Every write SHALL pass through one write gate in `Wc3.Mcp`, which resolves the output path, applies the refusal rules, creates the parent directory, writes and returns the digests
requirements.basis: Design decision. Today the rule is implemented twice, in `ResolveOutPath` and again inside several commands, so a new tool can miss it

requirements.statement: The write gate SHALL refuse an output equal to the input, an output inside an input folder map, and an existing output unless the caller passes `overwrite` true. It SHALL NOT refuse a new file in the input's folder
requirements.basis: Measured. `WriteGate.Save` refuses all three with `OUT_PATH_IS_INPUT`, `OUT_PATH_INSIDE_INPUT` and `OUTPUT_EXISTS`, and a replacement needs the flag and the user's grant. 61 writing tools pass the caller's flag through instead of hardcoding true, so a rerun that would overwrite is refused at the surface

requirements.statement: A write result SHALL report `savedTo`, `inputSha256`, `outputSha256`, `filesRewritten` and `bytesWritten`, so a caller can verify what changed and chain the next edit on the right file. `filesRewritten` proves the declared change size, not the preservation of the other entries, which the round-trip comparison and the write sweep establish
requirements.basis: Design decision. A count of rewritten internal files is available from the dirty set and is the cheapest fidelity signal a caller can get

requirements.statement: Every write SHALL accept an optional `expect_input_sha256` and SHALL refuse the call when it differs from the digest of the bytes it parsed. This verifies the input revision. It SHALL NOT be described as proof that the caller chose the latest output of a sequence
requirements.basis: Design decision. The parameter text already warns that two edits from one base lose the first. A digest turns a changed base into a refusal, and it cannot detect an unchanged base reused by mistake

requirements.statement: No tool SHALL overwrite its input map, model, texture or replay. A map edit with no `out_path` SHALL default to `<map>.edited.<ext>`, a port to `<target>.ported.<ext>`, and every other output SHALL be required
requirements.basis: Measured. The defaults exist and the parameter text states them. Two implementations, one gate

requirements.statement: An extract tool SHALL refuse a relative path that escapes its output folder, a rooted path, a drive letter, a device name and a `..` segment after normalization, applying one shared rule
requirements.basis: Measured. `mpq_extract_all` uses the same rule as the CLI `extract`. It is not applied to every folder-writing tool

requirements.statement: A destructive tool SHALL require `confirm` true and SHALL refuse the call with an error naming what would be removed when it is absent. A non-destructive write SHALL NOT require it
requirements.basis: Measured. The eleven tools that declare `destructiveHint` true take `confirm`, and `RunConfirmed` refuses a call without it as `CONFIRM_REQUIRED`, naming the item, before the map is even loaded. The other 107 writing tools do not take it

requirements.statement: A map, model, texture or report write SHALL stage to a temporary file in the destination folder and rename it into place, so a crash or a full disk cannot leave a truncated artifact where a valid one was. The client config writer already does this
requirements.basis: Measured. `MapDocument.WriteAtomically` writes a hidden staging file beside the destination, flushes it to disk and renames it over the destination, deleting the staging file on any failure. A test throws from an internal seam between the flush and the rename and proves the previous file is still byte for byte, and the test fails against the old direct write

requirements.statement: A tool SHALL NOT follow a symbolic link to write outside the folder the caller named, and a link in an extract destination SHALL be refused
requirements.basis: Design decision. The server writes where the caller says, not where a link points

requirements.statement: A batch write SHALL apply every edit in one load and SHALL write nothing when any edit fails. A partial batch SHALL NOT produce an output
requirements.basis: Measured. `ObjectBatchSetCommand` applies the edits to the loaded document in order, the first failure stops the run with the failing position, and the tool writes through the gate only when the result is Ok, so a failed batch creates no file. `ObjectBatchSetCommandTests` asserts both the stop and the absence of an output

requirements.statement: The write gate SHALL live in the shared layer and SHALL be reachable from the CLI, the Studio and MCP, so a guarantee does not depend on the front end
requirements.basis: Design decision. SUR-01 promises one behaviour per command, and SAF-04 places the gate in the adapter

requirements.statement: A tool that writes several files SHALL publish them as a unit, by a staged directory or a manifest written last, and SHALL NOT report success until every file is complete
requirements.basis: Design decision. An OBJ, MTL and texture set can be half written while each file is individually atomic

requirements.statement: A read-only audit SHALL report Channel-based abilities that share a Base Order ID, and SHALL distinguish levels that disagree and empty order ids
requirements.basis: Measured. `audit orders` finds 105 shared ids in Anime Choice Arena V0.33A and 53 in Anime WoS2 v0.34h

requirements.statement: A permission file SHALL be read at start from a path outside every folder the server writes, SHALL name the tools or families that need a person's approval and the tools that are refused outright, and a denied call SHALL fail with `POLICY_DENIED` naming the rule. A missing file SHALL deny nothing, and a malformed file SHALL refuse what it cannot classify
requirements.basis: Design decision. Adopted on 8 November 2026 from the Roblox Studio MCP server, where a file the agent cannot reach is the authority and `confirm` is only intent. Section 23.1 states the design

requirements.statement: `confirm` SHALL state intent and SHALL NOT grant permission. A denial in the permission file SHALL fail a call that carries `confirm` true, and the tool text SHALL say which of the two decides
requirements.basis: Design decision. SAF-10 already says a flag proves the caller included it, not that a person approved it, and today nothing else decides

requirements.statement: The server SHALL NOT collect telemetry, analytics or usage data, and SHALL NOT contact any endpoint that is not named in SEC-02
requirements.basis: Measured. A scan of the tree finds no analytics package, no telemetry call and no phone home. The only outbound addresses in code are the three retrieval downloads and the release check, both named in SEC-02, and the rest of the `https://` strings are documentation links printed by `clients`
requirements.test: measured against the tree and the published exe

requirements.statement: Every network access SHALL be listed here with its purpose, its trigger and its verification. Today there are four. `rag_install` fetches the model and the corpus. `update` fetches a GitHub release. The npm postinstall fetches the release archive. `install.ps1` fetches and unpacks a release
requirements.basis: Measured. The scan finds exactly those, the three retrieval URLs and the self-updater's release call in code, and the launcher and the installer script in the packages. Nothing else opens a socket
requirements.test: measured against the tree and the published exe

requirements.statement: Every download SHALL be verified against a pinned SHA-256 and, where a size is known, a size, and the RAG corpus SHALL be the fixed bundled dataset, never a folder named by the caller
requirements.basis: Measured. The model, the vocabulary and the dataset carry pinned SHA-256 constants, the launcher verifies the release archive against its published digest, the corpus URL is a fixed release asset, and `rag_install` takes only `threads` and `batch`, so no caller can name a folder
requirements.test: measured against the tree and the published exe

requirements.statement: The server SHALL NOT read, write or log a secret, a token, a credential or a connection string. A client config write SHALL add one MCP entry and nothing else
requirements.basis: Half met. A config write adds one entry and leaves every other key alone, which the setup tests prove. The graph store reads `NEO4J_PASSWORD` from the environment to connect to an optional local Neo4j, so one credential is read

requirements.statement: The threat model SHALL state that the boundary is the operating system account, that any client the user starts can call any tool, and that the server does not sandbox the client
requirements.basis: Measured. Section 6.11 now states all three, that the server runs as the signed-in user, that any client the user starts can call any tool, and that the server does not sandbox the client, then says what it does enforce, its own boundary
requirements.test: measured against the tree and the published exe

requirements.statement: A parser bug on a hostile map SHALL NOT execute code, write outside the output path or crash the process without a tool error
requirements.basis: Not measured. The design holds, managed code with no `eval` and no assembly loading, writes bounded by the gate, and a parser failure becomes a tool error in every case observed. No hostile input has been fed to it, so the claim rests on the design rather than on a run

requirements.statement: A resource read SHALL return a file from the installed `context/` folder and SHALL NOT accept a path from the caller
requirements.basis: Measured. `wc3://context/abilities` returns the shipped markdown, and `wc3://context/../../secret`, the same with an encoded traversal, and `file:///C:/Windows/win.ini` are all refused as unknown resources
requirements.test: measured against the tree and the published exe

requirements.statement: The parsers SHALL have a named fuzz corpus and a stated residual risk, and a malformed input SHALL return a tool error rather than terminate the process
requirements.basis: Design decision. Managed code, no `eval` and native CascLib are not a proof

requirements.statement: Both products SHALL offer `install`, `uninstall`, `config`, `clients`, `doctor`, `version`, `help` and `update`, and one implementation SHALL serve the CLI, the standalone exe and the Studio dialog
requirements.basis: Measured. `SetupCli.Verbs` holds all eight and the dispatcher handles each, `SetupProduct.Standalone` and `SetupProduct.Wc3ctl` both run through the same `SetupCli.Run`, and the Studio dialog calls it with an entry override. `Help_and_version_name_the_command_that_was_typed` pins the naming

requirements.statement: Every supported client SHALL have a fixture test that starts from a temporary home, runs install, checks the written entry, runs uninstall and checks it is gone
requirements.basis: Measured. `Every_client_round_trips_from_a_temp_home` does install, read back and uninstall over the nine clients that write a file, and `Claude_code_uninstall_runs_its_own_remove` covers the one that is set up through its own CLI. Every fixture runs against a temp profile, so no real client config is read or written

requirements.statement: A client config SHALL be backed up before a write, written atomically, and comments in it SHALL survive the write. A file that cannot be parsed SHALL be refused, with the snippet printed instead
requirements.basis: Measured. The backup suffix is asserted after a write, the replacement is atomic, and a config with line and block comments keeps every one of them. A file that is not valid JSON is left byte for byte and the refusal names it

requirements.statement: A PATH edit SHALL preserve every other entry exactly as written, including `%VARIABLES%` and the registry value kind
requirements.basis: Measured. `Path_entries_written_with_variables_stay_unexpanded` proves a `%VAR%` entry survives unchanged, and `A_folder_already_on_path_through_a_variable_is_not_added_twice` proves the same entry is not duplicated. The raw read and write are what make this hold

requirements.statement: `--npx` and `WC3_MCP_NPX=1` SHALL register the auto-updating `npx -y wc3-mcp@latest` command, and a plain install SHALL register the absolute exe path
requirements.basis: Measured. `Npx_option_registers_the_auto_updating_npx_launcher` pins the npx command, and the plain install path is asserted in every round-trip test as the absolute command

requirements.statement: `doctor` SHALL check the exe, `CascLib.dll`, the context folder, the game directory, each client entry, the version against the latest release when the network is available, and SHALL exit non-zero on a problem
requirements.basis: Measured. The published `doctor` prints the program, `CascLib.dll`, the context folder with one line per document and skill, the game folder, every client, and the release. On 8 November 2026 it reported `0.5.19 is available, you are on 0.4.13` as a warning and still exited 0, with every context item present

requirements.statement: Install and uninstall SHALL be idempotent, and a second install SHALL leave exactly one entry
requirements.basis: Measured. `Installing_twice_changes_nothing_the_second_time` proves the second write is a no-op, and the Claude Code path runs `mcp remove` before `mcp add` so its entry cannot multiply

requirements.statement: Setup SHALL NOT require administrator rights and SHALL NOT write outside the user profile, the user PATH and the exe folder
requirements.basis: Half measured. The fixtures write only into a temp profile and the PATH writer targets the user PATH, which needs no elevation. No test proves that nothing was written outside those places, so the boundary rests on the paths the code chooses

requirements.statement: An unknown client or an unknown option SHALL exit 2, name the legal set and print the snippet, rather than exiting 0
requirements.basis: Measured. `Unknown_client_and_unknown_option_are_usage_errors` asserts exit 2 for an unknown client, an unknown option and a missing client. The unknown client message names every legal id, and the missing client path prints the client list and the example command

requirements.statement: Uninstall SHALL remove only this product's entry and its own PATH folder, and SHALL NOT remove another product's entry with the same name
requirements.basis: Measured. Removal is by name only, never by command or by folder, and `Uninstall_removes_only_this_server` proves a foreign entry in the same file survives. The PATH folder is removed only on `uninstall --all`

requirements.statement: A client whose config file cannot be parsed SHALL be reported, not overwritten. The other clients SHALL still be set up
requirements.basis: Measured. A broken file leaves the file byte for byte, exits 1 and names the parse failure, and `A_broken_file_does_not_stop_the_other_clients_in_an_all_install` proves the clients that are fine are still written in the same `--all` run

requirements.statement: Every tool that acts on a map, a model, an asset, a script or a replay SHALL be a thin wrapper over one `Wc3.Commands` handler. The introspection tools and the reference search MAY live in the MCP layer, and no tool in that layer SHALL parse a map format, a model, a script or an archive, or reimplement logic the shared layer owns
requirements.basis: Measured. This is the architecture today and the reason the CLI, the Studio and MCP cannot drift in behaviour. Two tools are introspection (`mcp_audit_annotations`, `version_info`) and one is the lexical reference search (`docs_search`), which lives in `Wc3Context` over the shared heading rule

requirements.statement: A tool name SHALL follow `<domain>_<verb>[_<noun>]`, lower case, one canonical name per operation, and the verb SHALL be the operation rather than a synonym. `map_info` and `map_info_get` SHALL NOT both exist. `list_files` and `file_list` SHALL NOT both exist
requirements.basis: Measured. Both pairs exist today, plus `triggers_read` beside 25 `trigger_*` tools, `placed_units_list` beside `placed_unit_*`, and `search` beside `docs_search`

requirements.statement: A renamed tool SHALL keep an alias for at least one minor release, the alias SHALL say it is deprecated and name the replacement, and `wc3://tools` SHALL list the replacement. The alias may be removed in the first major release after the rename, never in a minor release
requirements.basis: Design decision. An agent may have a cached prompt that names the old tool, and a hard removal turns that into a failed task

requirements.statement: One operation SHALL have one tool. A tool that only reformats another tool's result SHALL be a parameter of that tool, unless it answers a different question
requirements.basis: Measured. `leak_list` is a presentation over `script_leaks`, and `map_overview` is a composition of three reads. The second is justified, the first is a candidate to merge

requirements.statement: Every description SHALL state what the tool does, whether it writes, what it refuses and the one trap a caller would otherwise hit, in at most 600 characters. The longer rationale SHALL live in the generated reference and in `tool_help`
requirements.basis: Measured. Two descriptions exceed 1,000 characters and the surface totals about 20,000 tokens before the user asks anything

requirements.statement: Every tool SHALL belong to exactly one family, and the family SHALL be visible in the catalog resource and the generated reference
requirements.basis: Measured. `McpToolFamilies` holds the inventory, 275 tools across the eleven families in section 6.5, and the catalog carries the family for each tool. `Every_tool_belongs_to_exactly_one_family` fails on a tool with no family, so a new tool cannot land ungrouped

requirements.statement: The full surface SHALL stay under 300 tools and under 70,000 characters of description text. A profile named `core` SHALL offer the read, inspect, audit and single-map edit tools for a client with a small context, and the default SHALL remain the full surface
requirements.basis: Measured. The surface is 275 tools and 84,315 characters today, so the 300 tool ceiling is a guard against growth and the 70,000 character ceiling is a cut of 14,315 characters

requirements.statement: No tool SHALL require more than eight parameters, and a requirement for more SHALL become a parameter object with its own schema
requirements.basis: Measured. The maximum is eight today, `force_set_flags`. More than that is where a model starts inventing values

requirements.statement: Every parameter SHALL have a type, a description and, when it is optional, a stated default. An enumerated value SHALL list its legal values in the description and SHALL NOT accept an unknown one silently
requirements.basis: Measured. All parameters are typed and described today, and most enums are listed. PAR-05 makes the refusal uniform

requirements.statement: Every tool SHALL carry a `title` annotation, a short human label, so a client can show a readable name without parsing the description
requirements.basis: Design decision. No tool sets a title today, and a client that displays one falls back to the snake case name

requirements.statement: Every command in `Wc3.Commands` that writes a map, a model or a script SHALL be reachable from the CLI and from the MCP surface, or the parity map SHALL name it and state why it has no front end. A command with tests and no front end SHALL NOT be counted as shipped
requirements.basis: Measured. `SoundScriptSpliceCommand` inserts a generated dispatcher into `war3map.j` and has eight tests, three of them pjass facts, and it has no CLI verb and no tool, so the only caller is the test suite

requirements.statement: The server SHALL speak MCP over stdio as newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout, one process per client, started by the client
requirements.basis: Measured. Every measurement in this document talks to the published server that way, one child process per client, a JSON line out for a JSON line in. Records like TRN-02 and OBS-01 below are captured the same way

requirements.statement: stdout SHALL carry protocol messages only. Every log line, banner and warning SHALL go to stderr
requirements.basis: Measured. At debug the server wrote 89 lines to stderr, the banner and the log records among them, and every line it wrote to stdout parsed as JSON. A stray banner would have failed the parse

requirements.statement: The server SHALL exit 0 when stdin closes, and SHALL finish the in-flight call before exiting where the client allows it
requirements.basis: Half measured. The process exits 0 within 0.4 s of stdin closing. A call in flight at that moment is abandoned, not finished, so a client that closes the pipe during a write gets no result and cannot tell whether the write happened

requirements.statement: Every call SHALL load its inputs, do its work and return, with no session state carried between calls other than caches documented in OBS and PRF
requirements.basis: Measured. Two `map_overview` calls in one process, on two different maps, returned two different results with nothing carried across. Every tool loads its own inputs on the call and none of them keeps a map between calls

requirements.statement: The server SHALL declare only the capabilities it has, and SHALL NOT advertise `listChanged` for a collection that cannot change during a session
requirements.basis: Measured. All three collections advertise `listChanged` true while the surface is fixed at start. Setting `Capabilities` to false in `CreateOptions` does not change the reply, because the pinned SDK 1.4.1 derives the capabilities from the registered collections and ignores the options, proven by a handshake test that fails on the configured value. The change lands in the SDK pin (CMP-02) or a wrapper, not in this repository

requirements.statement: The server SHALL NOT add a network transport in version 1. If one is added later it SHALL require authentication, an explicit workspace root and a separate specification
requirements.basis: Structural. The published server takes one transport, stdio, and the tree holds no listener of any kind, no `HttpListener`, no `TcpListener`, no Kestrel host, so there is no socket to authenticate

requirements.statement: A second server instance SHALL be safe. Two clients may start the server at once, and neither may hold a lock that blocks the other, except a short lock on the RAG index build
requirements.basis: Measured. Two instances started at the same moment, both initialised, both answered a call, and neither created a lock file beside the exe

requirements.statement: The protocol tests SHALL drive the real server wiring through an in-memory client, covering initialize, tools/list, one real call, one error, the catalog resource, a prompt and a context resource
requirements.basis: Measured. `McpServerTests` drives the real wiring and covers all seven, initialize with identity, the tool list, `list_files` round tripping a real map, a missing map as a clean error, the catalog resource as JSON, a prompt round trip, and the context documents as resources

requirements.statement: Every read-only tool SHALL be called against synthetic maps built in the test, with no real map and no game install required, and the result SHALL be JSON that parses and carries its documented fields
requirements.basis: Measured. The current sweep is corpus-gated and selects by name prefix, so a write tool with a read-like name escapes it

requirements.statement: Every writing tool SHALL be called into a temporary folder with minimal valid arguments, the output SHALL load, the input digest SHALL be unchanged, and the tool SHALL refuse an output equal to its input
requirements.basis: Design decision. This is the test that would have caught the class of defect the tool safety tests were written for

requirements.statement: The annotation audit SHALL fail on a tool with no hints, a read-only name that declares `destructiveHint` true, a writing name that declares `readOnlyHint` true, and a destructive tool that declares false
requirements.basis: Measured. The audit fails a tool with no hints, a tool that leaves any hint unset, a mutating name marked read-only, a writing tool that says read-only, a tool that declares both read-only and destructive, and a tool whose only effect is removal but declares non-destructive. Two of the latter found real defects, `mpq_remove` and `mpq_remove_many`, now corrected

requirements.statement: Every tool SHALL have a CLI parity entry, and a new tool SHALL fail the parity test until one is added
requirements.basis: Measured. `CliMcpParityTests` asserts both directions, `Every_mcp_tool_has_a_real_cli_command` and `Every_cli_command_is_mapped_or_allowlisted`, and `Mapping_covers_exactly_the_real_mcp_tool_set` fails the moment a tool exists without a mapping
requirements.test: the suite named in the basis

requirements.statement: The generated references SHALL be regenerated in memory and compared byte for byte with the committed files
requirements.basis: Measured. `DocsReferenceTests` renders both documents from the live tree in memory, reports the first differing line, and the committed file is the comparison
requirements.test: the suite named in the basis

requirements.statement: The setup writers SHALL be tested over a temporary home, a temporary app data and a temporary PATH for every client, including the comment refusal, the backup and the idempotence
requirements.basis: Measured. `SetupTests` runs every fixture over a temp home, temp app data and a temp PATH, and asserts the comment handling, the backup file and that a second install changes nothing, plus a round trip per client
requirements.test: the suite named in the basis

requirements.statement: The npm launcher SHALL be tested for its version path with no download, its cache hit, a digest mismatch, a network failure and the stdout rule
requirements.basis: Measured. `npm/test/launcher.test.js` runs nine tests on `node --test`, covering all five and four stdout subtests, against a temporary cache with the network stubbed at the fetch boundary, and the launcher itself is unchanged

requirements.statement: Each family SHALL have a result size test, asserting the documented page and the cap
requirements.basis: Not implemented. No test asserts a page size and a cap per family, so the result limits in RES-03 have no guard

requirements.statement: A hermetic test SHALL NOT depend on a map outside the repository and MAY build a synthetic map in a temporary folder. The Corpus category SHALL be excluded from the hermetic run
requirements.basis: Measured. The categories exist, `Corpus`, `GameData` and `Doctor`, and the CI command runs `Category!=Corpus&Category!=GameData&Category!=Doctor`. The hermetic fixtures build their maps in a temporary folder
requirements.test: the suite named in the basis

requirements.statement: Every error code SHALL have a test that produces it, and the code list test SHALL fail when a new code appears without a test
requirements.basis: Design decision. An error code path that never ran is a guess

requirements.statement: A pull request that changes the surface SHALL fail CI when the count in the README, the generated reference or this specification disagrees with the live count
requirements.basis: Design decision. DOC-03 and DOC-01 without a check are intentions

requirements.statement: The MCP and setup suites SHALL run on Windows in CI on every pull request, and a corpus run SHALL be available by hand
requirements.basis: Measured. The workflow runs on `windows-latest` for every push to the two long lived branches and every pull request against `master`, and the hermetic filter runs the MCP, setup and map suites in about three seconds
requirements.test: the suite named in the basis

requirements.statement: Each write family SHALL have a semantic test that asserts the intended change and the preservation of unrelated data, not only that the output loads
requirements.basis: Design decision. A model with missing UVs and a map with a wrong trigger subtree both load

requirements.statement: A test of a generator SHALL assert the generator's own output. It SHALL NOT rename, rewrite or normalise that output before asserting, and a repair a test needs SHALL be fixed at the source instead
requirements.basis: Measured. The splice test renamed a parameter and repaired an escaped path before asserting, so pjass proved a repaired block while both defects stayed in the generator. Both were fixed on 8 November 2026 and the repairs were removed. `SoundScriptSpliceCommandTests` and `SoundImportCommandTests` pass, 12 tests between them

gaps.what: No tool publishes an output schema, and no result carries structured content
gaps.where: Tool creation options and the result POCOs

gaps.what: No result size limit. `list_files` has `brief` and `docs_search` cuts at 1,600 characters, and nothing else has a bound
No progress notification and no cancellation token, on a surface that includes folder audits and model import
gaps.where: Tool signatures and the long commands

gaps.what: `file_get_text` decodes UTF-8 with replacement characters, silently, and no tool extracts raw bytes
19 descriptions exceed the 600 character cap and two exceed 1,000, while 33 are under 150 and do not state a trap
The surface is 275 tools and 84,315 characters, with no profile
gaps.where: The surface builder and a profile filter

gaps.what: Nine names need a canonical rename, including one true duplicate pair, `list_files` and `file_list`
gaps.where: `Wc3Tools`, the alias table, the parity map

gaps.what: No tool has a title annotation
The output rule is implemented twice, in `ResolveOutPath` and again inside several commands
gaps.where: One gate in `Wc3.Mcp` and the command defaults

gaps.what: 61 writing tools return the digests, a rewritten count and bytes through the gate. The remaining 57 writing tools write directly and carry none of it
gaps.where: The write gate, one family at a time

gaps.what: 61 writing tools accept `expect_input_sha256`. The remaining 57 cannot refuse a call whose input changed after it was read
gaps.where: The write gate, one family at a time

gaps.what: No error carries a code and there is no documented code set
No error code has a test
The two documents are served whole and there is no section resource
This specification is not served as a resource
No `tool_help`, so the long rationale has nowhere to live once descriptions are capped
gaps.where: A new tool and the generated reference

gaps.what: Every collection advertises `listChanged` true while nothing changes at run time. `McpServerOptions.Capabilities` is set to false and the pinned SDK 1.4.1 ignores it, so this is blocked on the SDK pin rather than on this repository
gaps.where: The `ModelContextProtocol` pin, or a wrapper that rewrites the reply

gaps.what: Six live artifacts carry five different versions, and the published npm package is 0.5.19 while the mirror's newest tag is v0.5.16 and its tree says 0.5.16 and 0.5.8, so the tree and the tags cannot reproduce what a user installs
gaps.where: Both `Directory.Build.props`, npm, mcpb, `server.json`, the tag, CI

gaps.what: The read sweep selects read-only tools by name prefix and needs a real map, so a write tool with a read-like name escapes it
No test calls every writing tool, checks that the output loads, or checks that the input is unchanged
The generated MCP reference carries no parameters, no result shape and no error codes
The catalog carries no aliases and no input schema, so a client cannot check what it is about to call without a second request
gaps.where: The catalog record and the resource

gaps.what: No map or archive list tool has `limit` or `offset`. `list_files` has `brief` and the graph tools have a count limit, and an object list or a script function list is still returned whole

The counts guard runs in the PDF build and cannot run in CI yet. A job pointed at the mirror's own exe fails on a correct tree, because that checkout builds 267 tools and 3 resources against the 275 and 6 this document describes
The changelog ignores requirement IDs and the breaking-change marker, and a non-conventional commit falls under other without failing anything
A changelog entry is not produced or committed by the release, so the notes can lag the tag
No watch mode rebuilds, tests, regenerates docs and publishes on a change
gaps.where: A new command and the publish script

gaps.what: No release-readiness command folds the existing gates into one verdict
`publish-all.ps1` is PowerShell only, is not run by CI, and neither tests nor regenerates the docs
A local publish is not verified by starting the exe, and only the release does that
gaps.where: The publish script and the smoke script

gaps.what: `docs` and the publish script answer no `--json`, so an agent cannot drive them from one shape
Nothing checks the committed changelog against the commits since the last tag
The capability catalogue in section 14 is hand-written and can drift from the surface. Nothing generates it and the counts guard does not read it
gaps.where: A generated capability map from the tool families

gaps.what: The document cites no external source, so a basis that claims a protocol rule or a client behaviour cannot be checked by its reader
gaps.where: Appendix D and the Basis column

gaps.what: The body numbers are guarded by `measure_surface.py` and `check_counts.py` at build time and by nothing in CI, so a pull request can move the surface without failing
The package and the model export publish as a unit. The asset and model converters still write several files directly, with no staged directory or manifest
No explicit limit exists on entry count, decompressed bytes, parser depth, array size or child-process time
gaps.where: The loader, the commands and the host

gaps.what: PRF-05 counts the input and output bytes and ignores parsed sections, assets, schemas and concurrent calls
No artifact records its commit, digest and tag, and npm 0.5.19 has no tag that explains it
gaps.where: The release workflow and the mirror

gaps.what: The write sweep asserts that an output loads, not that the intended change is present and the rest is preserved
No fuzz corpus runs against the archive, object, trigger or script parsers
gaps.where: The test suite and the native reader

gaps.what: `SoundScriptSpliceCommand` has eight tests and no CLI verb and no tool, so nothing a caller can reach writes the generated dispatcher into `war3map.j`
No permission file exists, so the only thing that stops a destructive call is the caller's own `confirm` flag, and nothing the user writes can refuse a tool
gaps.where: A new policy type, the host, and section 23.1

gaps.what: Every skill is served by no resource. The two reference documents are readable and a skill is not
A cold start to the initialize reply is 1.2 seconds against the 1 second requirement. The start line costs 0.03 seconds of it, so the cost is the host building the surface and the SDK handshake
195 of the 202 `map` parameter descriptions do not say whether a folder map is accepted. Seven do, all in the Lua and script family

The mirror checkout builds 267 tools and 3 resources against the 275 and 6 the specification documents. Eight tools are absent, `audit_ability_orders`, `content_scaffold`, `hero_generate`, `model_primitive`, `model_squish`, `object_batch_set`, `object_fix_model_ext` and `sound_import_events`, so the export has not been run since they landed
The prompt list is not in the catalog resource, so a client that reads the catalog cannot see what a prompt takes without a second request
gaps.where: The catalog record and the prompt list

gaps.what: No tool refuses or warns before reading when the game install is absent, and `gamedata_enum` returns `entries: []` when no schemas were found, with no note that it searched nothing
No tool reports a partial success. The batch tools refuse instead, so the rule has no implementation and no test
No test scans an error message for a path, an input or leaked content, and a call that fails schema validation returns a message naming none of them
gaps.where: The error paths and the contract tests

gaps.what: A context resource reports its MIME type and its description but not its byte size
No resource reports a byte size or a SHA-256, so a client cannot tell a truncated copy from the shipped one
An in-flight call is abandoned when stdin closes, so the exit is clean but the work is lost with no result to the client
No per-call log line carries a duration or a result size, so the one line a slow-client report needs does not exist
No test fails when a log line carries content it should not, so the rule rests on reading the calls
gaps.where: The logging middleware and the tests

gaps.what: A tool error is logged by the generic handler as an unhandled exception at debug, without its code, rather than once at warn
No test proves setup writes nothing outside the user profile, the user PATH and the exe folder, so the boundary rests on the paths the code chooses
A release note never names a requirement id or a defect, so a reader cannot tell which rule a change serves
No convention marks a breaking change in a release note, a tool description or this document, and no tool is marked deprecated
gaps.where: The changelog entries and the tool descriptions

gaps.what: Nothing checks the platform before the server starts, so a non-Windows or ARM user meets the operating system's error for a Windows executable rather than a sentence naming `win-x64`
No game directory tool marks a degraded field when the install is absent, so a base name reads as an absence of data
gaps.where: The 36 tools that take a game directory

gaps.what: `gamedata_enum` accepts an unknown type and returns an empty set instead of refusing and naming the legal values
Eight of the nine array parameters state no maximum, and no call above a limit is proven to be refused rather than truncated
The graph store reads `NEO4J_PASSWORD` from the environment, so the server does read one credential, and nothing documents or bounds that read
No hostile input has been fed to the parsers, so the claim that a parser bug cannot escape rests on the design rather than on a run
gaps.where: The parsers and the fuzz corpus

gaps.what: No test asserts a page size and a cap per family, so the result limits have a rule and no guard
